# Aunt Euphemia

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v3 c16 P52](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0052)</sub>
- **Role:** housemother  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c35 P5](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0005)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Aunt Phemie  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>; Aunty  <sub>[v3 c25 P3](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0003), [v3 c35 P2](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0002)</sub>

## Appearance

Aunt Euphemia is a small, elderly woman with a gently triangular face. She has rose-colored cheeks, large and tender blue eyes filled with youthfulness, and silver-white hair styled in small rolls above her ears.

_Sources: [v3 c16 P52](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0052)_

## Personality

Aunt Euphemia is a good-humoured, happy woman who lives by the doctrine of serving God and others while enjoying life. She possesses a youthful spirit and laughing eyes, acting as a affectionate and graceful housemother to the girls residing at Tabby's Place. Though she holds firm ideas on propriety, she can be completely won over by constant, respectful manners.

_Sources: [v3 c16 P51](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0051), [v3 c18 P2](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0002), [v3 c19 P4](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0004), [v3 c26 P18](../source/v03-c26.md#nw-v03-c26-p0018), [v3 c35 P5](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0005)_

## Traits

- happy  <sub>[v3 c19 P4](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0004)</sub>

- cooking  <sub>[v3 c27 P6](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0006)</sub>

## History

Aunt Euphemia was named Jamesina after her father James, who drowned at sea shortly before her birth. After her only daughter Elizabeth married and went to the foreign mission field in India, Aunt Euphemia moved to Portmaris to keep house for Nell Harcourt, Honora, and their friends at Tabby's Place. Bringing her pet Sarah-cat with her, she served as a housemother for three winter seasons, hosting the students and offering warm guidance. Despite a deep fear of snakes in India, she eventually traveled there to investigate her daughter's mission field.

_Sources: [v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c16 P23](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0023), [v3 c16 P51](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0051), [v3 c16 P58](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0058), [v3 c18 P25](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0025), [v3 c37 P12](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0012), [v4 c3 P16](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0016)_

## Background by volume

- father James drowned a month prior to her birth  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>
- grew up in a family with around six girls  <sub>[v3 c19 P41](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0041), [v3 c19 P42](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0042)</sub>
- always desired a yellow silk dress but was forbidden from having one by her mother and husband  <sub>[v3 c19 P6](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0006)</sub>
- used to laugh at and mock her suitors  <sub>[v3 c35 P21](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0021)</sub>
- advised a suitor to wear an elastic strip to flatten his ears  <sub>[v3 c37 P40](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0040)</sub>
- received the Sarah-cat as a gift from her laundress  <sub>[v3 c16 P58](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0058)</sub>
- taught her daughter to cook before allowing her to attend university  <sub>[v3 c27 P6](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0006)</sub>

## Quotes

> Fulfill what you owe to God, to those around you, and to yourself, while enjoying your life. Such is the doctrine I live by, and it has served me quite effectively.  <sub>[v3 c19 P4](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0004)</sub>

> Obtaining a yellow silk dress is the absolute first action I intend to take upon arriving in heaven.  <sub>[v3 c19 P6](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0006)</sub>

> Deriding your suitors lacks propriety; however, it was my own constant habit.  <sub>[v3 c35 P21](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0021)</sub>

> That young man should wear an elastic strip around his skull at night so his ears learn to lie flat.  <sub>[v3 c37 P40](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0040)</sub>
